entities.summary: The Basrah Museum is a museum in the Iraqi city of Basra, It is located on the banks of the Shatt al-Arab some 3 km south‐east of Basra’s historic city centre. Housed in a former palace of Saddam Hussein, its collection is related to Mesopotamian, Babylonian, Persian civilisations, as well as the history of the city itself. Basrah Museum opened its doors to the public in March 2019. The Director of the Basrah Antiquities & Heritage is Qahtan Al Abeed, who has managed the project from the start with the cooperation of the State Board of Antiquities & Heritage and the Ministry of Culture and with support from the UK Friends of Basrah Museum (FOBM).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Basrah Museum's collection of Mesopotamian and Babylonian artifacts provides a unique window into the history of the region, shedding light on the cultural exchange between ancient civilizations. Its establishment has contributed to the preservation of Iraq's cultural heritage.
